page: Amazon Web Services c7a.medium is an entry-tier compute-optimized server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. It utilizes a single dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 physical core running at a 3.7 GHz clock speed with one thread per core. The instance is equipped with 2.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware feature flags include AVX-512 extensions (AVX512F, VNNI, BF16), AES cryptography instructions, and SHA extensions, alongside 4 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache per core. The server includes no local NVMe storage and reports a baseline network throughput of 0 Gbps.

In performance benchmarks, the c7a.medium demonstrates strong single-core CPU throughput, reaching the top 25 percent in stress-ng evaluations with a score of 3031.18. Single-threaded Geekbench execution yields an average rating, alongside an average text generation speed of 107.26 tokens per second on small 135M parameter language models. However, overall multi-core and memory bandwidth scores fall into lower percentiles due to the single-core hardware ceiling. Uncached memory read bandwidth tests register at 34.27 GB per second, while compiled software generation and image processing workloads show restricted capacity under multi-threaded stress testing.

From an infrastructure perspective, the c7a.medium offers high single-thread processing capabilities relative to its baseline hardware profile. Because memory capacity is capped at 2.0 GB and multi-core scalability is absent, cost efficiency relies on isolating non-parallelized tasks that benefit from modern instruction sets like AVX-512 without requiring concurrent execution threads. Appropriate workloads for this instance profile include single-threaded background jobs, lightweight web serving utilities, basic text processing scripts, and low-scale utility microservices.
